check_connection.description: Check the museum's Open Access API is answering and report how much is in it: how many works are catalogued, how many have been photographed, how many are hanging in the galleries today, and how many artists and exhibitions there are. Worth putting at the front of a workflow that will act on a count, and a quick way to see the connection is working.
check_connection.display_str_template: Check the Cleveland Museum of Art connection.

mock_response.authentication: None. The Open Access API is keyless and read only.
mock_response.licence: The data is CC0. Images are CC0 for works whose licence reads CC0, which is about three in five of them; the rest are still in copyright and are described but not pictured.
mock_response.source: The Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API

description: Search and read the Cleveland Museum of Art's collection: 68,000 catalogued works with the museum's own commentary, their provenance, their exhibition history, and published pictures of 41,000 of them at web, print and archival resolution. Find what is hanging in the galleries today, pull a piece of the collection at random for a daily post, look up the artists and the biographies the museum has written for them, or read through the 5,700 exhibitions it has staged since 1879. The data is public domain and about three works in five carry a CC0 picture that can be reused anywhere without asking. No account or key required.
